standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness of the base changed morphism, and flatness of the induced morphisms of small etale sites
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, labels spaces-morphisms-lemma-base-change-flat (invoked at proof line 1950) and spaces-morphisms-lemma-flat-morphism-sites (invoked at proof line 1953)
standard_prerequisites.use: They show that $g'$ is flat and that flatness of $g$ and $g'$ is the flatness of the corresponding morphisms of small etale ringed sites, which is what the base change map requires.

standard_prerequisites.name: The base change map for a flat morphism of sites
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology on Sites, label sites-cohomology-lemma-base-change-map-flat-case (invoked at proof line 1956)
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the map $g^*R^pf_*\mathcal{F} \to R^pf'_*\mathcal{F}'$ whose bijectivity is the content of part (1).

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the higher direct images of the affine morphism $g'$, with Leray
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-affine-vanishing-higher-direct-images (invoked at proof line 1977) and Cohomology on Sites, label sites-cohomology-lemma-apply-Leray (invoked at proof line 1979)
standard_prerequisites.use: They give $H^p(X_B, \mathcal{F}_B) = H^p(X, g'_*\mathcal{F}_B)$, because $g'$ is affine as a base change of the affine morphism $\Spec(B) \to \Spec(A)$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Lazard's theorem, writing a flat algebra as a filtered colimit of finite free modules
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, label algebra-theorem-lazard (invoked at proof line 1997)
standard_prerequisites.use: It provides the filtered system of finite free $A$-modules $M_i$ with $B = \colim M_i$, over which the tensor product and the cohomology can be moved.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a quasi-compact quasi-separated space commutes with filtered colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-colimits (invoked at proof line 2014)
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the third equality in the chain, and it is what allows the colimit to be moved out of the cohomology of the tensor product.

core_obligations: Establish that $g'$ is flat and that the flatness of $g$ and $g'$ agrees with the flatness of the induced morphisms of small etale sites, so that the base change map $g^*R^pf_*\mathcal{F} \to R^pf'_*\mathcal{F}'$ is available (proof lines 1949-1960).

Reduce the bijectivity of that map to the affine case by working locally in the etale topology on $Y'$, and translate it into statement (2): the map $H^p(X, \mathcal{F}) \otimes_A B \to H^p(X_B, \mathcal{F}_B)$ is an isomorphism (proof lines 1961-1970).

Use affineness of $g'$ to get $H^p(X_B, \mathcal{F}_B) = H^p(X, g'_*\mathcal{F}_B)$, and compute $g'_*\mathcal{F}_B = \mathcal{F} \otimes_{\underline{A}} \underline{B}$ by evaluating on an affine $U$ etale over $X$ (proof lines 1972-1995).

Write $B = \colim M_i$ as a filtered colimit of finite free $A$-modules and compute the cohomology by moving the colimit and the tensor product inside, using that cohomology commutes with filtered colimits and with finite direct sums, to reach $H^p(X, \mathcal{F}) \otimes_A B$ (proof lines 1995-2018).
proof_roadmap: Flatness of the base change and the base change map (proof lines 1949-1960).
Reduction to affine $Y$, $Y'$ and the translation into (2) (proof lines 1961-1970).
The affine $g'$ and the description of $g'_*\mathcal{F}_B$ (proof lines 1972-1995).
The colimit computation with Lazard's theorem (proof lines 1995-2018).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the flat base change theorem in the setting of algebraic spaces: the base change map on higher direct images is an isomorphism for a flat morphism of the base, with the affine form identifying the cohomology after a flat base change with the tensor product (statement lines 1921-1946). The proof produces the base change map from the flat case for morphisms of sites, reduces the question to an affine base, computes the pushforward along the affine base change explicitly, and evaluates the resulting cohomology by expressing the flat algebra as a filtered colimit of finite free modules and moving colimits through cohomology. The colimit computation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
